column2: In positional number systems, each digit must be smaller than the base. Binary 102 is invalid because binary allows only 0 and 1. Octal 78 is invalid because octal allows only 0 to 7. Hexadecimal 1G is invalid because hexadecimal allows 0 to 9 and A to F. Decimal 29 is valid.

The same written digits can represent different values depending on the base. The number 10 in binary equals decimal 2; 10 in octal equals decimal 8; 10 in decimal equals decimal 10; and 10 in hexadecimal equals decimal 16. Always state the base when comparing numbers.
To convert binary 101101 to decimal, use place values 32, 16, 8, 4, 2, and 1 from left to right. The calculation is 32 + 0 + 8 + 4 + 0 + 1 = 45. Therefore 101101 base 2 equals 45 base 10.

Convert decimal 25 to binary by repeated division: 25 divided by 2 gives quotient 12 remainder 1; 12 gives quotient 6 remainder 0; 6 gives quotient 3 remainder 0; 3 gives quotient 1 remainder 1; and 1 gives quotient 0 remainder 1. Read the remainders from bottom to top to obtain 11001. Reading them from top to bottom is incorrect.
Octal place values are powers of 8. To convert 157 base 8 to decimal, calculate 1 times 64 plus 5 times 8 plus 7 times 1. The result is 64 + 40 + 7 = 111. Therefore 157 base 8 equals 111 base 10.

To convert decimal 83 to octal, repeatedly divide by 8. The first division gives quotient 10 remainder 3; the second gives quotient 1 remainder 2; the third gives quotient 0 remainder 1. Read the remainders from bottom to top. Therefore decimal 83 equals octal 123.
In hexadecimal, F represents decimal 15. To convert 2F to decimal, calculate 2 times 16 plus 15 times 1. The result is 47. Therefore 2F base 16 equals 47 base 10.

To convert decimal 156 to hexadecimal, divide by 16. The quotient is 9 and the remainder is 12. The hexadecimal digit for 12 is C. Therefore decimal 156 equals hexadecimal 9C. Check the result using 9 times 16 plus 12 = 156.

column1: Grouping binary digits and padding zeros
column2: For the integer part of a binary number, group bits from the binary point towards the left. Use groups of three for octal and four for hexadecimal. Add leading zeros only when needed to complete the leftmost group. Binary 11010 becomes 011 010, which is octal 32; or 0001 1010, which is hexadecimal 1A. Adding trailing zeros to an integer changes its value.

Convert decimal 0.625 to binary by multiplying the fractional part by 2: 0.625 times 2 = 1.25, so record 1; 0.25 times 2 = 0.5, so record 0; 0.5 times 2 = 1.0, so record 1 and stop. Read these recorded digits in their original order. Therefore decimal 0.625 equals binary 0.101.

Binary 101.01 contains both an integer part and a fractional part. Calculate 1 times 4 plus 0 times 2 plus 1 times 1 plus 0 times one-half plus 1 times one-quarter. The result is 5.25 in decimal. The first position after the binary point represents one-half, not one-tenth.

column1: Binary addition rules and worked example
column2: Binary addition follows these rules: 0 + 0 = 0; 0 + 1 = 1; 1 + 0 = 1; and 1 + 1 = 10, meaning write 0 and carry 1. With an incoming carry, 1 + 1 + 1 = 11, meaning write 1 and carry 1. Binary 1011 + 0110 = 10001. In decimal, this is 11 + 6 = 17.

In binary subtraction, 0 minus 1 requires borrowing from a higher position. A borrowed 1 from the next position contributes binary 10, which is decimal 2, to the current position. For example, binary 1010 minus 0011 equals 0111. This agrees with decimal 10 minus 3 equals 7.

To represent negative 5 in eight-bit twos complement, first write positive 5 as 00000101. Invert all eight bits to obtain 11111010, then add 1 to obtain 11111011. Therefore 11111011 represents negative 5 when interpreted as an eight-bit twos complement integer. The bit width and signed interpretation must be specified.

The same bits can have different meanings depending on their interpretation. The eight-bit pattern 11111111 represents 255 as an unsigned integer, but negative 1 as a twos complement integer. Eight-bit unsigned integers range from 0 to 255. Eight-bit twos complement integers range from negative 128 to positive 127.

To calculate 9 minus 5 using eight-bit twos complement, write 9 as 00001001 and 5 as 00000101. The twos complement of 00000101 is 11111011. Adding 00001001 and 11111011 gives 1 00000100. Keep the lower eight bits and discard the carry beyond eight bits. The result is 00000100, which is decimal 4.

Decimal 25 is 0010 0101 in standard 8421 BCD because decimal digit 2 becomes 0010 and digit 5 becomes 0101. The pure binary representation of decimal 25 is 11001. Interpreting 00100101 as pure binary gives decimal 37, so BCD and pure binary must not be confused. Valid four-bit 8421 BCD digit codes range from 0000 to 1001.

Decimal 26, binary 11010, octal 32, and hexadecimal 1A represent the same numerical value. Binary 11010 equals 16 + 8 + 2; octal 32 equals 3 times 8 plus 2; hexadecimal 1A equals 1 times 16 plus 10. Each calculation gives decimal 26.
